COLD CLEAR AIR: sharp and bracing, every distant ridge reading crisp, the tonal steps between planes precise and clean
DRY CLEAR AIR: bone-dry and still, distances compressing into clear flat layers, each receding plane holding its edge firmly
WASHED CLEAN AIR: rain-rinsed freshness hanging everywhere, the atmosphere pellucid, far details emerging with unusual sharpness and fidelity
THIN HIGH-ALTITUDE AIR: rarefied and spare, offering little to soften edges, far peaks reading almost as close as near ones
WARM STILL AIR: heavy and languid, holding a gentle luminous quality, the distance softening only slightly into tender pale warmth
CLEAR AIR WITH LIGHT BREEZE: fresh and moving gently, carrying just enough stir to keep edges clean and distances bright
VALLEY MIST: a low white mist pooled along the valley floor, thinning as it rises, the upper slopes clear above it
LOW FOG BANK: a dense white layer sitting flat across the middle distance, upper forms floating free above its smooth surface
SEA FOG: a thick grey-white mass rolling in from the water, softening the coastline and dissolving the furthest forms entirely
MORNING HAZE: a soft pearlescent veil hanging close to the ground, blurring the bases of forms while their tops stay readable
DUST HAZE: a fine ochre-tinted suspension dulling the air, flattening contrasts and wrapping the distance in a warm tawny glow
HEAT HAZE: shimmering and trembling just above the ground, making the lowest band of the distance ripple and swim visibly
DUST DRIFT: a loose pale suspension carried on a dry wind, laying a chalky bloom across the middle and far distances
DRIZZLE VEIL: a fine grey curtain of thin rain moving across the distance, merging forms into soft indistinct tonal masses
THIN RAIN VEIL: a translucent scrim of falling moisture, cool and grey, softening all edges beyond the immediate foreground
DRIFTING RAIN CURTAIN: a slow-moving sheet of fine rain crossing the landscape, dulling colour and drawing forms toward a unified grey
SNOW FLURRY: a swirling scatter of fine flakes thickening the air, reducing the distance to a pale indeterminate whitish blur
BLOWING SNOW: driven horizontally on a hard wind, streaking the air white and erasing the far distance into flat brightness
GROUND DRIFT: loose dry snow lifted and carried low across the surface, veiling the base of forms in a thin white rush
SEA SPRAY: a fine salty mist thrown up from breaking water, hanging in the air and softening everything in the near distance
WATERFALL SPRAY: a perpetual drifting cloud of fine moisture, cool and white, blurring the immediate surroundings in a luminous vaporous bloom
COASTAL SPRAY HAZE: a persistent salt-laden mist clinging to the air above the shore, giving the near distance a soft silvery diffusion
DISTANT WILDFIRE SMOKE: a brownish haze thickening toward the horizon, absorbing the far distance into a warm murky amber depth
WOOD SMOKE HAZE: a thin blue-grey scrim of smoke settling across the middle distance, lending a soft hazy blue to receding forms
DISTANT SMOKE PALL: a broad flat layer of grey-brown smoke spreading across the far distance, compressing tonal range and muting all colour
